# Cipi

> Cipi is a free, open-source (MIT) platform that turns a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 or 26.04 VPS into a hardened hosting server for Laravel and PHP apps, with zero-downtime Git deploys, an optional self-hosted web panel, a REST API and MCP servers for AI assistants. A self-hosted alternative to Laravel Forge, Ploi and Vito Deploy: no subscription, nothing leaves your server.

Install: `wget -O - https://cipi.sh/setup.sh | bash` (as root on a fresh server). Then log in as `cipi` and run `sudo cipi …`.

## Key facts

- **Free and self-hosted.** MIT licence. No account, no SaaS control plane, no telemetry. The only cost is the VPS.
- **Isolated apps.** Each app gets its own Linux user, PHP-FPM pool (`open_basedir`), database user, Nginx vhost, certificate and deploy key.
- **App types.** Laravel (PHP-FPM or Octane with FrankenPHP), Node apps (SPA, static, SSR with Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Astro, Remix, Vite), and custom PHP apps (WordPress, Symfony, static sites).
- **Zero-downtime deploys.** Deployer releases with one atomic symlink swap, `cipi deploy <app> --rollback`, pre-deploy DB snapshots, health-checked automatic rollback, a hash-chained deploy audit trail. Push-to-deploy from GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps (automatic setup with a token) or any Git server.
- **cipi.yml.** An app's server settings in its repository: PHP version and ini, aliases, www/apex, workers, Horizon, Reverb, scheduler, Meilisearch, health check, deploy options and post-deploy steps, extra databases, crons, backup profiles, redirects, proxies, Node settings. `cipi yml plan` shows every change; `apply` is all-or-nothing; `auto on` applies after every deploy. `cipi-<env>.yml` per environment (the server chooses the file). Fail-closed: namespaced resources, allowlisted runners, no secrets.
- **Runtime.** Several PHP versions side by side (8.3–8.6; new servers default to 8.6), MariaDB (default) and optional PostgreSQL, one Valkey instance per app, optional Meilisearch, Node runtimes, Supervisor workers, Horizon, Reverb behind the app's own domain, Octane with pinned FrankenPHP builds, per-app JIT.
- **Security.** SSH keys only, UFW, fail2ban (configurable attempts), optional CrowdSec, Cloudflare Zero Trust (tunnel, Access, close ports), encrypted vault (AES-256) for credentials, nightly PHP patching from packages.sury.org at 03:30 with alerts while a version is vulnerable, nginx from nginx.org mainline with `cipi autoupdate`, HTTP/2 never enabled, hardened PHP-FPM admin flags, malware scans, compliance reports.
- **Operations.** Backup profiles to local and S3-compatible destinations (encrypted, retention, verification), `cipi sync` to move or replicate apps between servers, server monitor, health checks, disk usage per app and database, notifications by e-mail, Slack, Discord, Telegram, Mattermost, Google Chat, ntfy, Pushover or webhook.
- **Interfaces.** CLI first. Optional web panel (`cipi gui <domain>`): fleet view of many servers, roles and per-app permissions, invite links, TOTP 2FA, OpenID Connect SSO. REST API (`cipi api <domain>`) with Sanctum tokens and abilities, IP allowlist, Swagger. cipi-cli (Go binary for your laptop), PHP SDK (`cipi/sdk`), WHMCS module.
- **AI.** Two MCP servers: the Cipi Agent's per-app MCP (`composer require cipi/agent`, `/cipi/mcp`: health, logs, DB schema and capped queries, Artisan, deploy, cipi.yml validation; SQL and Artisan guards, secret redaction) and the server MCP of the API (`/mcp`). Plus a GDPR-safe database anonymizer.
- **Requirements.** Full VM or bare metal (KVM, VMware, Hyper-V, Xen HVM), Ubuntu 24.04 or 26.04 LTS, public IPv4, ports 22, 80, 443. Not for local Docker, WSL or LXC.

## Site

English only, unprefixed URLs. Web panel: https://cipi.sh/web-panel — REST API: https://cipi.sh/api — MCP for AI: https://cipi.sh/mcp — Docs: https://cipi.sh/docs/ — Guides: https://cipi.sh/guides/ (RSS: https://cipi.sh/guides/feed.xml) — Comparisons: https://cipi.sh/alternatives — cipi.yml: https://cipi.sh/cipi-yml — Source: https://github.com/cipi-sh — News: https://t.me/cipicloud

## Documentation


### Start here

- [Quickstart](https://cipi.sh/docs/quickstart): From a fresh VPS to a Laravel app on HTTPS in five commands.
- [Install Cipi](https://cipi.sh/docs/installation): Server requirements, SSH keys, the installer and first login.
- [How Cipi works](https://cipi.sh/docs/how-cipi-works): The stack Cipi installs and how each app is laid out on disk.

### Apps

- [Create an app](https://cipi.sh/docs/create-app): The cipi app create wizard and its flags for Laravel, Node and custom apps.
- [Laravel Octane](https://cipi.sh/docs/octane): Run apps on FrankenPHP, convert existing apps and pin builds.
- [PHP JIT per app](https://cipi.sh/docs/php-jit): Turn the OPcache JIT on or off for a single app.
- [Node apps](https://cipi.sh/docs/node-apps): SPA, static and SSR frontends built on every deploy.
- [Custom PHP & static sites](https://cipi.sh/docs/custom-apps): WordPress, plain PHP and SFTP-only sites.
- [Manage apps](https://cipi.sh/docs/manage-apps): List, inspect, edit, clone and delete apps; set a default app.
- [Environment variables](https://cipi.sh/docs/environment): Read and change an app's .env safely.
- [Queues & Horizon](https://cipi.sh/docs/workers): Supervisor workers and Laravel Horizon per app.
- [Scheduler & cron](https://cipi.sh/docs/scheduler): The Laravel scheduler and each app user's crontab.
- [Reverb WebSockets](https://cipi.sh/docs/reverb): Enable Laravel Reverb behind Nginx for an app.
- [Limits & suspension](https://cipi.sh/docs/limits): Cap CPU, memory and disk per app; suspend and resume apps.
- [Basic auth](https://cipi.sh/docs/basic-auth): Password-protect an app behind HTTP basic auth.
- [Artisan, commands & logs](https://cipi.sh/docs/artisan-logs): Run Artisan, Tinker and shell commands; read app logs.
- [SSH as the app user](https://cipi.sh/docs/app-ssh): SFTP and SSH access for each app's own Linux user.

### Deploy

- [How deploys work](https://cipi.sh/docs/how-deploys-work): The deploy paths Cipi supports and when to use each.
- [Deploy & roll back](https://cipi.sh/docs/deploying): cipi deploy, releases, rollback, status and logs.
- [Git providers & deploy keys](https://cipi.sh/docs/git): GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps and more — keys and webhooks set up for you.
- [Auto-deploy on push](https://cipi.sh/docs/auto-deploy): The signed webhook that deploys when you push.
- [CI/CD pipelines](https://cipi.sh/docs/ci-pipelines): Deploy from GitHub Actions, GitLab CI or any pipeline over SSH.
- [cipi.yml](https://cipi.sh/docs/yml): Configuration that travels with your code.
- [Customize the pipeline](https://cipi.sh/docs/deploy-script): Deploy options and your own Deployer tasks.
- [Safe deploy & DB snapshots](https://cipi.sh/docs/safe-deploy): Back up before a release and snapshot the database before migrations.
- [Deploy audit ledger](https://cipi.sh/docs/deploy-audit): A hash-chained record of who deployed what, and from where.
- [Preview environments](https://cipi.sh/docs/preview-environments): A live copy of the app for every branch.
- [Deploy notifications](https://cipi.sh/docs/deploy-notifications): Hear about successful and failed deploys.

### Domains & SSL

### Server & runtime

- [Uninstall](https://cipi.sh/docs/uninstall): Remove Cipi from a server.

- [SSH keys](https://cipi.sh/docs/ssh-keys): Add, list and remove admin SSH keys.
- [Vault & encryption](https://cipi.sh/docs/vault): AES-256 encryption at rest for configs, tokens and keys.
- [CrowdSec](https://cipi.sh/docs/crowdsec): Opt-in IP reputation and community blocklists.
- [Cloudflare Zero Trust](https://cipi.sh/docs/zero-trust): Reach SSH through Cloudflare and close port 22.
- [Malware scan](https://cipi.sh/docs/malware-scan): Nightly scans of app files.
- [Compliance evidence](https://cipi.sh/docs/compliance): ISO 27001 and SOC 2 checks and reports.

- [Database anonymizer](https://cipi.sh/docs/anonymizer): Copy production data without personal data.
- [Agent security & ENV](https://cipi.sh/docs/agent-config): Tokens, IP rules and every ENV variable.

## Guides


### Get started

- [Deploy Laravel on an Ubuntu VPS with zero downtime](https://cipi.sh/guides/deploy-laravel-ubuntu-vps): From a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 or 26.04 server to a Laravel app on HTTPS with queues, scheduler and push-to-deploy, explained from zero: install, create the app, connect Git, deploy, HTTPS, rollbacks and the first-day problems.
- [Move a Laravel app from Forge (or Ploi) to Cipi](https://cipi.sh/guides/migrate-from-laravel-forge): A step-by-step migration from Laravel Forge or Ploi to a free, open-source Cipi server: mapping each Forge feature to its Cipi equivalent, a fresh server, the app, the .env, the database, files, workers and scheduler, a DNS switch with almost no downtime, and a rollback plan.
- [VPS, SSH and DNS for Laravel developers who never ran a server](https://cipi.sh/guides/vps-ssh-dns-basics): The words and the three skills you need before deploying to your own server, explained from zero: what a VPS is, choosing one, creating an SSH key, logging in, pointing a domain with DNS records, checking it worked, and what Cipi takes care of so you don't have to.

### Cloud providers

- [Install Cipi on AWS EC2](https://cipi.sh/guides/cipi-aws-ec2): Launch an AWS EC2 instance for Laravel step by step (Ubuntu AMI, instance type, gp3 storage, security group, Elastic IP), install Cipi, point DNS, and connect S3, SES and CodeCommit.
- [Install Cipi on Amazon Lightsail](https://cipi.sh/guides/cipi-aws-lightsail): Create an AWS Lightsail instance for Laravel step by step (OS-only Ubuntu blueprint, plan, static IP, IPv4 and IPv6 firewall), install Cipi, point DNS and know when to move to EC2.
- [Install Cipi on a DigitalOcean Droplet](https://cipi.sh/guides/cipi-digitalocean): Create a DigitalOcean Droplet for Laravel step by step (image, size, SSH key, cloud firewall, reserved IP), install Cipi, point DNS, and use Spaces for off-site backups.
- [Install Cipi on Hetzner Cloud](https://cipi.sh/guides/cipi-hetzner): Create a Hetzner Cloud server step by step (location, Ubuntu image, server type, SSH key, firewall, IPv4), install Cipi, point DNS and set up off-site backups to Hetzner Object Storage.
- [Cipi on Vultr, Akamai Linode, OVHcloud and Scaleway](https://cipi.sh/guides/cipi-vultr-linode-ovhcloud): Install Cipi on Vultr, Akamai Linode, OVHcloud, Scaleway or any provider: what to choose, provider by provider, a checklist for unknown providers, and fixes for the usual first-day problems.

### Laravel

- [A Laravel API with a Next.js or Nuxt front end on one server](https://cipi.sh/guides/laravel-api-nextjs-nuxt): Run a Laravel API and a server-rendered Next.js or Nuxt front end side by side, each with its own domain, zero-downtime deploys and HTTPS, plus Sanctum for authentication.
- [CI/CD for Laravel with GitHub Actions or GitLab CI](https://cipi.sh/guides/laravel-ci-cd-git-workflow): Test on every push and deploy only when tests pass, with automatic rollback, a restricted CI key, an optional backup step and zero-downtime releases.
- [The self-hosted Laravel developer stack (2026)](https://cipi.sh/guides/laravel-developer-stack-2026): Which parts of a Laravel team's toolchain are worth owning (servers, deploys, backups, search, analytics, error tracking) and which are still better bought, with the cost math.
- [The Laravel ecosystem in 2026, mapped to production](https://cipi.sh/guides/laravel-ecosystem-2026): Octane, Horizon, Reverb, Scout, Pulse, Livewire, Filament, Inertia, Pest and the rest, grouped by the job they do, with what each one needs from your server.
- [Laravel .env and secrets in production, done right](https://cipi.sh/guides/laravel-env-secrets): What the .env file is, why it never goes in Git, where Cipi keeps it so it survives deploys and rollbacks, how to change values safely from the CLI, the panel or the API, rotating database passwords and API keys, config caching, and keeping secrets out of logs and AI tools.
- [Laravel queues and Horizon in production](https://cipi.sh/guides/laravel-horizon-queues): Queues explained from zero, then everything for production on your own server: what a worker is, adding and scaling queues under Supervisor, timeouts and retries, switching to Horizon on Valkey, protecting the dashboard, deploys that never run old code, failed jobs, alerts and cipi.yml.
- [Multi-tenant Laravel SaaS with wildcard subdomains](https://cipi.sh/guides/laravel-multi-tenant-wildcard): Build a SaaS where every customer gets their own subdomain, explained from zero: how wildcard DNS, routing and certificates fit together, setting them up with Cloudflare and Cipi, resolving the tenant in Laravel, custom domains for customers, and when to give a tenant its own app instead.
- [Laravel Octane with FrankenPHP on your own server](https://cipi.sh/guides/laravel-octane-frankenphp): Serve Laravel from memory with Octane and FrankenPHP, side by side with PHP-FPM apps, with pinned builds, safe upgrades and zero-downtime reloads.
- [Laravel on PostgreSQL, on your own server](https://cipi.sh/guides/laravel-postgresql): From zero to a Laravel app on PostgreSQL with Cipi: what Postgres is good at, installing it next to MariaDB, creating apps and extra databases on it, connecting from your laptop, backups, restores, upgrades and moving an existing app from MySQL.
- [Preview environments for every Laravel branch](https://cipi.sh/guides/laravel-preview-environments): Give every branch its own live URL with a database, workers and HTTPS, created on the first push and deleted with the branch, using GitHub Actions and a wildcard certificate.
- [Real-time Laravel with Reverb, on your own domain](https://cipi.sh/guides/laravel-reverb-websockets): Run Laravel Reverb WebSockets behind your app's own domain and certificate, with Supervisor, Nginx and Echo configured for you. No extra ports, no Pusher bill.
- [Laravel scheduler and cron jobs in production](https://cipi.sh/guides/laravel-scheduler-cron): How Laravel's task scheduler works on a server, explained from zero: the one cron line, how Cipi runs it per app, writing scheduled tasks that don't overlap, running them on one server only, extra cron jobs, alerts when a job fails and how to debug one that never ran.
- [Laravel Scout with Meilisearch, self-hosted](https://cipi.sh/guides/laravel-scout-meilisearch): Add fast, typo-tolerant search to a Laravel app with Scout and a Meilisearch instance on your own server, isolated per app, with no Algolia bill.
- [Laravel cache, sessions and queues on Valkey (Redis)](https://cipi.sh/guides/laravel-valkey-cache-sessions): What Redis and Valkey are, when to move Laravel's cache, sessions and queues off the database, and how to do it on Cipi with one isolated Valkey instance per app: switching drivers, memory limits, eviction, moving off a shared instance, and debugging.
- [Zero-downtime Laravel deploys with safe migrations](https://cipi.sh/guides/laravel-zero-downtime-migrations): How atomic releases work, how to write migrations that never break the live release, and how to take a database snapshot and roll back automatically when something goes wrong.

### cipi.yml

- [cipi.yml recipes for common Laravel setups](https://cipi.sh/guides/cipi-yml-recipes): Copy-paste cipi.yml files for a SaaS with Horizon and Reverb, an API with Octane, a multi-tenant app on a wildcard domain, a site with redirects and a Next.js front end.
- [Staging and production from one repository with cipi.yml](https://cipi.sh/guides/cipi-yml-staging-production): A beginner-friendly walkthrough to run a staging copy and a production copy of the same Laravel app, each deploying its own branch with its own settings, driven by cipi-staging.yml and cipi.yml.
- [cipi.yml: keep your server settings in the repository](https://cipi.sh/guides/manage-apps-with-cipi-yml): Keep PHP, workers, scheduler, domains, databases, health checks, backups and deploy options in a cipi.yml next to your Laravel code, explained from zero: generate it, edit it, validate it, review it in pull requests, plan and apply it safely.

### Cipi Agent & AI

- [Anonymize a Laravel database with Cipi Agent, step by step](https://cipi.sh/guides/anonymized-database-dumps): Give developers, QA, staging and AI assistants a realistic copy of production with every personal field replaced, explained from zero: install the agent, scan the schema, review the rules, request a dump from your laptop, import it, and keep it GDPR-safe.
- [Monitor a Laravel app's health with the Cipi Agent and any uptime service](https://cipi.sh/guides/cipi-agent-health-monitoring): Expose a token-protected health endpoint covering database, cache, queue, storage and the last deploy, and plug it into UptimeRobot, Better Stack, Grafana or a cron.
- [Cipi Agent: connect your Laravel app to its server](https://cipi.sh/guides/cipi-agent-laravel-mcp): Install cipi/agent to get push-to-deploy, a health endpoint, an MCP server for AI assistants, cipi.yml validation and GDPR-safe database dumps in any Laravel app.
- [Push-to-deploy Laravel from GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket or Gitea](https://cipi.sh/guides/cipi-agent-webhook-deploy): Deploy on every git push with signed webhooks verified inside your app, branch filtering, an audit trail of who pushed, and deploys that never run inside a web request.
- [Manage Laravel in production with Claude, Cursor and the Cipi MCP](https://cipi.sh/guides/cipi-mcp-ai-agents): Connect Claude Code, Cursor or VS Code to your live Laravel app and to your server through Cipi's two MCP servers, with tokens, guardrails, secret redaction and an audit trail.
- [Spec-driven development with AI agents in Laravel](https://cipi.sh/guides/spec-driven-development-ai-laravel): Write the spec first, let an agent implement it against tests, and close the loop on production through MCP, with guardrails that keep data and deploys safe.

### Security

- [Put a Laravel server behind Cloudflare Zero Trust](https://cipi.sh/guides/cloudflare-zero-trust-laravel): Serve apps through a Cloudflare Tunnel with CDN and WAF, put staging, the panel and SSH behind Cloudflare Access, then close the server's public ports, step by step and reversibly.
- [Laravel production security checklist](https://cipi.sh/guides/laravel-security-checklist): A practical checklist for a Laravel app on your own server, covering the app, the PHP and nginx stack, access, data and monitoring, with the command that covers each item.
- [How Cipi handled the November 2026 PHP and nginx CVEs](https://cipi.sh/guides/php-nginx-cve-patching): A real case study of the nginx 1.31.9 and PHP 8.x security releases of November 2026: which CVEs reached a Cipi server, which were closed by default settings, and how servers were patched without downtime.

### Operations

- [Back up Laravel apps and databases to S3, and restore them](https://cipi.sh/guides/backup-vps-s3): Encrypted, scheduled backups of every app and database to AWS S3 or any S3-compatible storage (Hetzner, DigitalOcean Spaces, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, MinIO), with retention, verification and a tested restore.
- [The Cipi web panel and REST API](https://cipi.sh/guides/cipi-gui-and-api): Add an optional, self-hosted web panel for your team and clients, a REST API for automation, a CLI client for your laptop, and roles, 2FA and SSO, without giving up the terminal.
- [Move Laravel apps to a new server with cipi sync](https://cipi.sh/guides/migrate-server-cipi-sync): Migrate one app or a whole server between providers (AWS to Hetzner, an old VPS to a bigger one) with encrypted archives, the same deploy keys, database and storage, and a DNS switch when you're ready.
- [Server notifications: Telegram, Slack, e-mail and webhooks done right](https://cipi.sh/guides/notifications-alerts): Set up Cipi notifications from scratch, explained for beginners: which channels exist, which events trigger them, how to route urgent alerts to your phone and the rest to a quiet channel, how to verify signed webhooks, and how to avoid alert fatigue.
- [Upgrade PHP for a Laravel app without downtime](https://cipi.sh/guides/php-version-upgrade): How PHP versions work on a server, explained from zero: running several versions side by side, checking your code and Composer dependencies, moving one app at a time with zero downtime, rolling back, nightly security patches, end-of-life versions and Octane's own PHP.
- [Server monitoring and alerts on Telegram, Slack and e-mail](https://cipi.sh/guides/server-monitoring-alerts): Watch CPU, memory, disk, services, certificates and app health on your own server, and get alerted on Telegram, Slack, e-mail or a webhook when something actually breaks.

### PHP, WordPress & e-commerce

- [Deploy a Symfony app on an Ubuntu VPS with Cipi](https://cipi.sh/guides/deploy-symfony): Host Symfony as a custom app with the public/ document root, Composer and cache warm-up after each deploy, a database, Messenger workers via cron, HTTPS and backups.
- [Host WordPress on your own VPS next to Laravel apps](https://cipi.sh/guides/deploy-wordpress-custom-app): Run WordPress as an isolated custom app with its own PHP pool, database, HTTPS, backups and Git or SFTP deploys, on the same server as your Laravel apps.
- [Self-host PHP e-commerce on a VPS: Bagisto, Lunar, Sylius, PrestaShop and more](https://cipi.sh/guides/php-ecommerce-vps): A practical map of open-source PHP shop platforms and how to run each on your own server with Cipi, explained for beginners, with full setups for a Laravel-based shop (Bagisto) and a Symfony-based one (Sylius), plus what every shop needs.
- [WooCommerce on your own VPS, step by step](https://cipi.sh/guides/woocommerce-vps): Host a WooCommerce shop on an Ubuntu VPS from zero, explained for beginners: an isolated app, the database, HTTPS, PHP limits for a shop, real cron for Action Scheduler, caching, frequent backups, a staging copy and security.

## Comparisons

- [Cipi vs 20i](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-20i): 20i is a hosting company with reseller, WordPress and cloud plans; Cipi is free software for deploying Laravel and PHP on a VPS you own.
- [The best Laravel Forge alternatives in 2026](https://cipi.sh/best-laravel-forge-alternatives): Free and paid alternatives to Laravel Forge for deploying Laravel, grouped by model (self-hosted panels, SaaS panels, managed platforms, Docker platforms), with prices and who each one suits.
- [Cipi vs Cleavr](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-cleavr): Cipi is a free, self-hosted alternative to Cleavr for Laravel teams: zero-downtime deploys, an optional self-hosted panel, cipi.yml and MCP, with no subscription.
- [Cipi vs CloudPanel](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-cloudpanel): Two free server panels compared: CloudPanel for mixed PHP, Node and Python sites, Cipi for Laravel and PHP apps with zero-downtime deploys, cipi.yml and MCP.
- [Cipi vs Coolify](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-coolify): Two free self-hosted platforms compared: Coolify deploys containers for any stack; Cipi runs Laravel and PHP natively with zero-downtime releases, cipi.yml and MCP.
- [Cipi vs cPanel](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-cpanel): cPanel is built for selling shared hosting; Cipi is a free platform for deploying Laravel and PHP apps on your own VPS.
- [Cipi vs DirectAdmin](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-directadmin): DirectAdmin is a lighter shared-hosting panel; Cipi is a free platform for deploying Laravel and PHP apps on your own VPS.
- [Cipi vs Dokku](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-dokku): Dokku is a git-push Docker PaaS on your server; Cipi is a native Laravel and PHP platform with full server management, cipi.yml and MCP.
- [Cipi vs Easypanel](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-easypanel): Easypanel is a Docker-based server panel; Cipi runs Laravel and PHP natively with zero-downtime releases, cipi.yml and MCP.
- [Cipi vs fortrabbit](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-fortrabbit): fortrabbit is a managed PHP platform; Cipi is free software for running Laravel and PHP on your own VPS with full root.
- [Cipi vs Kamal](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-kamal): Kamal deploys containers to servers you prepare; Cipi provisions the whole Laravel stack and deploys natively, with backups, patching and MCP.
- [Cipi vs Laravel Cloud](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-laravel-cloud): Laravel Cloud is a fully managed, usage-based platform; Cipi is free software for your own VPS. Compare cost model, control, scaling and lock-in.
- [Cipi vs Laravel Forge](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-laravel-forge): Cipi is a free, self-hosted alternative to Laravel Forge: zero-downtime Laravel deploys, an optional web panel, cipi.yml, MCP for AI assistants and nightly security patching, with no subscription.
- [Cipi vs moss.sh](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-moss): Cipi is a free, self-hosted alternative to moss.sh: unlimited deploys, an optional self-hosted panel, cipi.yml and MCP, on your own VPS.
- [Cipi vs Plesk](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-plesk): Plesk is a general hosting panel; Cipi is a free platform for Laravel and PHP apps with zero-downtime deploys and cipi.yml.
- [Cipi vs Ploi Cloud](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-ploi-cloud): Ploi Cloud is a managed EU PaaS for Laravel, PHP and Node; Cipi is free software for your own VPS. Compare control, cost model and lock-in.
- [Cipi vs Ploi](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-ploi): Cipi is a free, self-hosted alternative to Ploi.io for Laravel and PHP: zero-downtime deploys, an optional self-hosted panel, cipi.yml, MCP and nightly patching, with no plan limits.
- [Cipi vs Render](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-render): Render is a multi-language managed cloud; Cipi is a free Laravel-first platform for your own VPS. Compare cost, control, previews and lock-in.
- [Cipi vs RunCloud](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-runcloud): Cipi is a free, self-hosted alternative to RunCloud with Laravel-native zero-downtime deploys, queues, Octane, cipi.yml and MCP, on any Ubuntu VPS.
- [Cipi vs ServerPilot](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-serverpilot): Cipi is a free alternative to ServerPilot with Laravel-native deploys, queues, SSL and security patching on any Ubuntu VPS.
- [Cipi vs Sevalla](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-sevalla): Sevalla is Kinsta's managed application platform; Cipi is free software for running Laravel and PHP on your own VPS.
- [Cipi vs Vito Deploy](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-vito-deploy): Two free, self-hosted server panels for Laravel and PHP compared: architecture, deploys, configuration as code, security patching, MCP and the web dashboard.
